---
title: "Reviewing Incident Reports"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Reviewing Incident Reports}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(eatPrep)

# Replay the interactive choices when building the vignette.
review_example <- function(dat, info) {
  answers <- c(rep("yes, all values", length(unique(info$issueId))), "yes")
  env <- new.env(parent = environment(visualSubsetRecode))
  env$.subset_menu <- function(choices) {
    if (!length(answers) || !answers[1] %in% choices) {
      stop("Unexpected example prompt.")
    }
    answer <- answers[1]
    answers <<- answers[-1]
    answer
  }
  review <- visualSubsetRecode
  environment(review) <- env
  invisible(capture.output(
    result <- suppressMessages(review(dat, info, toRecodeVal = "mci"))
  ))
  stopifnot(length(answers) == 0L, result$status == "completed")
  result
}
```

**You can process person-level, class-level, and mixed incident reports.** Each
row describes one incident affecting one person or one class. **A table can contain
reports for many people or classes.** A class report is reviewed as one incident,
even when it affects several people.

| Report type | `level` | `targetId` contains | Additional input |
|---|---|---|---|
| Person-level | `"person"` | The person ID for that row, e.g. `"P1"` | None for an item report |
| Class-level | `"class"` | The class ID for that row, e.g. `"K1"` | `persons`: the person-to-class mapping |
| Mixed: people and classes | `"person"` or `"class"` per row | The person or class ID for that row | `persons`: the person-to-class mapping |

"Mixed" describes a table containing both kinds of report. Each row still uses
`level = "person"` or `level = "class"`. See [workflow 3](#workflow-3-mixed-reports).

All three input options have the same steps: **describe the incident, check the selected
responses, then review and decide whether to recode them.**
`prepareSubsetInfo()` selects responses; `visualSubsetRecode()` opens the review.

Every issue table needs the same **five columns**: `issueId`, `level`, `targetId`,
`scope`, and `target`. Each `issueId` must be unique. The examples also include
the optional `comment` column; use `""` when no comment is needed. `head()` shows
the input table in each example.

## Shared example data

Three people answered two items. Use merged response data, before aggregating
subunits into items. In these examples, `"mci"` is the replacement code for
responses invalidated by an incident.

```{r responses}
review_data <- data.frame(
  ID = c("P1", "P2", "P3"),
  I1 = c(1, 0, 1),
  I2 = c(0, 1, 0)
)
review_data
```

## Workflow 1: person-level reports

**Example: display errors affected item I2 for P1 and P3.** Enter both reports in
one table, with a separate `issueId` for each. Set `level = "person"` and put
the affected person's ID in `targetId` on each row.

```{r person-input}
person_issues <- data.frame(
  issueId = c("V1", "V2"), level = "person", targetId = c("P1", "P3"),
  scope = "item", target = "I2", comment = c("Display error", "")
)
head(person_issues)
```

Resolve the affected responses:

```{r person-selection}
person_info <- prepareSubsetInfo(review_data, person_issues)
person_info[c("issueId", "ID", "datCols")]
```

The selection contains **P1/I2 and P3/I2**, reviewed as two separate incidents.
No class or booklet tables are needed.
Start the review in an interactive R session:

```{r person-review, eval=FALSE}
person_result <- visualSubsetRecode(review_data, person_info, toRecodeVal = "mci")
```

Choose **yes, all values** for each report, then **yes** to end the review.
The result is:

```{r replay-person, include=FALSE}
person_result <- review_example(review_data, person_info)
expected_person <- review_data
expected_person$I2 <- c("mci", "1", "mci")
stopifnot(identical(person_result$dat, expected_person))
```

```{r person-result}
person_result$dat
```

P1's and P3's responses to I2 change. P2's responses and all responses to I1
keep their original values.

## Workflow 2: class-level reports

**Example: a display error affected item I2 for everyone in class K1.** Set
`level = "class"` and put the class ID in `targetId`. Supply `persons` so the
function knows who belongs to that class:

```{r class-input}
persons <- data.frame(
  ID = c("P1", "P2", "P3"), classId = c("K1", "K1", "K2")
)
class_issue <- data.frame(
  issueId = "V3", level = "class", targetId = "K1",
  scope = "item", target = "I2", comment = ""
)
head(class_issue)
```

Resolve the affected responses:

```{r class-selection}
class_info <- prepareSubsetInfo(review_data, class_issue, persons = persons)
class_info[c("issueId", "ID", "datCols")]
```

The single class report selects **P1/I2 and P2/I2**. Both rows retain `issueId =
"V3"`, so you review them together and make **one decision for the class report**.
P3 belongs to K2 and is outside the selection.

```{r class-review, eval=FALSE}
class_result <- visualSubsetRecode(review_data, class_info, toRecodeVal = "mci")
```

Choose **yes, all values**, then **yes** to end the review:

```{r replay-class, include=FALSE}
class_result <- review_example(review_data, class_info)
expected_class <- review_data
expected_class$I2 <- c("mci", "mci", "0")
stopifnot(identical(class_result$dat, expected_class))
```

```{r class-result}
class_result$dat
```

The difference from workflow 1 is the affected people: **the same item is recoded
for everyone in K1**, while P3's responses stay unchanged. Class IDs must identify
classes uniquely across the data set, including across schools.

## Workflow 3: mixed reports

**Example: process the two person reports and the class report together.** Combine
them in one table. Each row keeps its own `level`, `targetId`, and unique `issueId`:

```{r combined-input}
issues <- rbind(person_issues, class_issue)
head(issues)
```

Supply the class membership table `persons`, as in workflow 2:

```{r combined-selection}
subset_info <- prepareSubsetInfo(review_data, issues, persons = persons)
summary(subset_info)
```

Start one review for the whole table:

```{r mixed-review, eval=FALSE}
mixed_result <- visualSubsetRecode(review_data, subset_info, toRecodeVal = "mci")
```

The review presents **V1 (P1), V2 (P3), and V3 (class K1)** separately. Choose
**yes, all values** for each report, then **yes** to end the review:

```{r replay-mixed, include=FALSE}
mixed_result <- review_example(review_data, subset_info)
expected_mixed <- review_data
expected_mixed$I2 <- rep("mci", 3)
stopifnot(identical(mixed_result$dat, expected_mixed))
```

```{r mixed-result}
mixed_result$dat
```

All three people's responses to I2 are recoded. P1/I2 occurs in both V1 and V3;
resetting one report keeps a recoding still required by the other. Choose
**reset to original values** to withdraw a previous recoding; **no** leaves it
unchanged. All three workflows preserve existing `NA` responses.

## If the incident affects a block

In all three workflows, `level` answers **who is affected?** and `scope` answers
**which responses are affected?** An item report uses `scope = "item"`. For an
entire block, also supply `booklets`, `blocks`, and `rotation`.

For example, P1 and P2 are both in K1 but use different block orders:

```{r block-design}
booklets <- data.frame(
  booklet = c("X", "Y"), block1 = c("A", "B"), block2 = c("B", "A")
)
blocks <- data.frame(
  subunit = c("I1", "I2"), block = c("A", "B"), subunitBlockPosition = 1
)
rotation <- data.frame(ID = c("P1", "P2", "P3"), booklet = c("X", "Y", "X"))
```

To report a problem with **the first block in class K1**, keep the class target
and change the scope to `"blockPosition"`:

```{r block-input}
block_issue <- class_issue
block_issue$scope <- "blockPosition"
block_issue$target <- "1"
head(block_issue)
```

```{r block-selection}
block_info <- prepareSubsetInfo(
  review_data, block_issue, persons = persons,
  booklets = booklets, blocks = blocks, rotation = rotation
)
block_info[c("ID", "datCols", "block", "blockPosition")]
```

This selects **P1/I1 and P2/I2**: the first block is A for P1 and B for P2.
Review `block_info` just like `class_info` above. To select **named block A**
instead, use `scope = "block", target = "A"`; that selects I1 for both people.

## Pause and continue

For a longer review, choose a new checkpoint filename when starting:

```{r checkpoint, eval=FALSE}
result <- visualSubsetRecode(
  review_data, subset_info, toRecodeVal = "mci", checkpoint = "review.rds"
)
# Choose "pause review (resume later)". In a later R session:
library(eatPrep)
result <- visualSubsetRecode(state = "review.rds")
```

Completed decisions are saved automatically. Resume with `state` to keep the
original values and earlier decisions. Continue your data preparation with
`result$dat`; `result$subsetInfo` contains the decision history.

For project data, the design tables can come from `inputList`. After
`recodeData()`, also pass `subunits = inputList$subunits` to map original item
names to recoded columns. See `?prepareSubsetInfo` and `?visualSubsetRecode` for
input requirements, review options, and checkpoint recovery.
